reviews.why: Copper traded at $6.08/lb on tradingeconomics.com on 2026-11-13, at or below the $6.15 kill level -- the same site had already flagged a four-month low of $6.20/lb on November 10. The slide was driven by Fed rate-hike pricing and a stronger dollar after hot US inflation data, not by anything happening at Escondida, so the kill condition fired on its own terms.

post_mortems.assumption_broke: The call assumed Escondida's regional output loss was, by itself, large enough to keep the global copper market tight and push a new record high. The global refined market was already running a surplus for most of 2026, so a real but regional disruption never had the leverage over price the thesis needed.
post_mortems.earlier_catch: ICSG's own global refined balance releases, public through the quarter (reported in roughly April, July/August and October 2026), kept showing a widening surplus. The hunt's checkpoints tracked only Escondida-specific output and labor news and never checked that global number against the thesis it was supposed to test.
post_mortems.rule: A thesis pinned to a single mine or region's supply disruption needs a checkpoint on the global refined balance, not only the regional disruption -- a tight region inside a confirmed global surplus will not move price on its own.

no_new_call_note: A scan across commodities, crypto and stocks this week turned up nothing both new and confirmed by more than one independent source that the market has not already priced: the Fed's rate-hike pricing after hot inflation data, China's tight physical copper market, the Escondida labor peace, and the DRC's copper-cobalt concentrate export ban are each already reported and already reflected in price, so no new call opens this week.
